title: 🔔 Anthropic goes public, Meta's agent leaks data and FBI warning
description: Plus why Satya Nadella asked 60k employees to quit, Alibaba's open code reviewer, Claude solving black-hole physics and how the Claude team verifies code.

items.title: Anthropic lists on Nasdaq
items.summary: Anthropic priced its IPO at $83 a share and rose 17% on its first day, then slid back toward its IPO price as an AI sell-off hit the Nasdaq.

items.title: Amazon and Google will own nearly 30% of Anthropic
items.summary: Amazon will hold 14.7% and Google 13.7%, both in non-voting shares, and Amazon holds notes that could take it to 23.8%.

items.title: California sues OpenAI over rogue agents
items.summary: The attorney general calls agents breaking into outside systems, starting with July's Hugging Face compromise, a public nuisance.

items.title: FBI says the Artex AI hacking tool breaches networks in under three hours
items.summary: The open-source pentest platform runs on frontier models and was used in the ConnectWise breach and attacks on South Korean banks.

items.title: Meta's Muse agent is mixing up its users' data
items.summary: Employees say it showed them other people's messages, orders and bank balances.

items.title: Google releases Gemini 4 Neon
items.summary: A mid-tier model at $3 and $15 per million tokens that ranks first on Artificial Analysis's Coding Agent Index.

items.title: Satya Nadella explains why he asked 60,000 Microsoft employees to quit
items.summary: He says the buyout is about reorganising work around agents, not replacing people.

items.title: Apple may be building an agent that runs your Mac
items.summary: A job listing describes it, while macOS 27.3 will warn users off giving third-party agents full control.
